history.summary: A Siddhapeeth Shakti shrine of Purnia said to be the only temple in the country believed to be the abode of all ten Mahavidyas of Goddess Bhagwati, and a popular venue for sanskar rituals (marriages, mundan). Local tradition makes it 500-600 years old: the saint Baba Hathinath cursed a Nawab's elephant that disturbed his bath (its tusks are still kept in a temple room), after which Nawab Shaukat Ali of Alamganj donated 4-5 acres of land — celebrated as Hindu-Muslim brotherhood. Some historians derive Purnia's name from the goddess; others say it comes from 'Poorn-Arnya' (complete jungle) — CONFLICT. A Rs 34-crore beautification/renovation was announced in 2025 news reports (verify). Coordinates are an approximate old-city (Syed Bara) point — geocoding unavailable; verify.

name: Puran Devi Mandir
town_description: Purnia (Purnea) is a major city of northeastern Bihar, often called 'Chhota Kolkata' for its Bengali cultural influence, and the headquarters of Purnia district and division. The Puran Devi temple stands in the old-city quarter (Syed Bara/Alamganj), described as about 5 km from the city centre in local guides.

travel.airport: Bagdogra (~140 km) or Patna; Purnia Airport has no verified commercial service (verify)
travel.railway: Purnea Junction (~4 km per a temple listing; verify)
travel.road: Old Purnia city (Syed Bara); NH-31/NH-27 link Purnia to the rest of Bihar and Bengal
